title: mini-phase-gap-injector-and-latency-phase-annotator
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: We've seen sporadic p95-p99 spikes in multi-tenant experiments that do not reproduce in synthetic steady-state runs. Root cause analysis points to short, phase-aligned scheduling gaps and micro idle windows between prime/warmup and steady token generation that break batching assumptions. This PR introduces a lightweight, deterministic 'mini-phase gap injector' into the bench runner and a companion 'latency phase annotator' for downstream reporters so we can (a) synthesize realistic micro-jitter between sequence phases, (b) label trace segments with phase metadata, and (c) export phase-aware latency deltas for attribution and visualization. Design summary: - gap injector: pluggable component for the Go bench runner (bench/runner/gap_injector.go). It supports configurable gap patterns: fixed, Poisson, and bursty windows. Gaps are expressed in microseconds and can target pre-token, between-token, and post-response boundaries. - deterministic mode: seedable RNG to ensure reproducible experiments across CI and local runs. - latency phase annotator: injects a thin annotation layer into the trace/telemetry pipeline (bench/reporters/phase_annotator.go) that records start/end times and sequence context for each phase (primer, warmup, steady, drain). - YAML experiment config: adds an opt-in section to existing workload descriptors to declare gap profiles and phase mapping. - CSV/Parquet export: reporter can emit per-sequence phase deltas so analysts can join with kernel-level telemetry. Backwards compatibility: gap injector is opt-in and disabled by default; no change to existing benchmark behavior unless a profile is specified. Checklist: - [x] gap injector implementation and unit tests - [x] phase annotator and reporter exports - [x] docs: README section with config examples and suggested profiling workflows - [x] added deterministic RNG seed option - [x] end-to-end example workload and CI smoke test Why this is different from prior work: existing tools focused on warmup and KV cache priming or large-scale bursts. This change targets short micro-gaps (10us-5ms) between logical phases which are not currently modeled. The goal is to detect fragile batching strategies and scheduler-induced tail effects before they hit production. How to use: add a `gap_profile` stanza to a workload YAML (examples provided in bench/examples/gap_profiles). Run `benchctl run --profile gap-mini` and the runner will emit phase-annotated CSV alongside standard latency histograms. Notes on measurement noise: small gaps can amplify measurement noise; the annotator includes an option to enable hardware timestamp alignment when available. Supporting artifacts and experiments are included in the PR and the README contains scripts used to reproduce the attached micro-experiments.

review_comments: Marco DeLuca: Nice addition — can we ensure the default profile is explicitly disabled so no CI job flips behavior unexpectedly?
Aisha Patel: Agree; injector is behind a feature flag and the CI smoke test flips it on only in a separate job. Added a note in the runbook.
Sofie Kwan: The Poisson generator uses float64; on very small mu values I saw drift in the test harness. Can we add a fixed-point fallback?
Aisha Patel: Switched critical path to integer microsecond math and added a fallback determinism mode. Tests updated.
Ravi Menon: CSV export is fine but can we add Parquet schema for later joins with kernel traces?
Aisha Patel: Added parquet export option behind `export_format` and included mapping in docs.
ci_summary: linux-unit-tests: pass; bench-smoke: pass; lint: pass; docs-build: pass; integration (gap-profile): pass
merge_outcome: squash-merge — PR merged by Marco DeLuca after approvals on 2025-11-26. Commit message consolidated to: 'mini-phase-gap-injector: simulate micro scheduling gaps and add phase annotator and exports'
release_notes: Adds an opt-in 'gap injector' for benchmark workloads that can synthesize short inter-phase scheduling gaps and a phase annotator that emits per-phase latency deltas for improved tail attribution. This is intended for advanced perf experiments and is disabled by default.
notes_for_oncall: If an alert spikes after enabling gap profiles, disable the profile and rerun baseline. Gap profiles are opt-in; do not enable on production benchmark pipelines without cross-team signoff.
how_to_reproduce: checkout feature branch; run `benchctl run --profile bench/examples/gap_profiles/gap-mini.yaml --out ./out && tail -n 200 ./out/phase_deltas.csv`
